run.why: EM-9 and EM-10 both require the same commit, host and window. Two separate runs would differ by exactly the run-to-run variance 4.4 records - 7.1x on this target - and the ratio between the regimes would be uninterpretable.

miss_body.statement: 60 KB of ordinary text carries no literal the Aho-Corasick prefilter can find, so the P1-7 skip FIRES and the full regex never runs. Asserted here, before any timing.

hit_body.statement: 40 KB of ordinary text containing a SQL-shaped substring. The prefilter ADMITS it, so the full regex RUNS. Asserted here, before any timing. The substring is benign and the endpoint is expected to serve the request - the property asserted is the PREFILTER'S, not a detection.

wire_bytes.statement: The SAME two properties asserted on the bytes the request actually carries - the JSON envelope, 41 bytes larger than the filler. The middleware scans request bytes, so this is the assertion the round-trip arm depends on. It is re-asserted rather than assumed because a body that changes class between the text and the wire would silently measure the wrong regime.

scan_cost.ceiling_basis: absolute, chosen BEFORE measurement, never relaxed
scan_cost.ratio_note: HIT/MISS at DIFFERENT body sizes. The hit body is SMALLER, so this ratio UNDERSTATES the per-byte penalty: the hit regime costs more while scanning 33% fewer bytes. Per-KB figures are reported beside it so the per-byte story is not hidden by the size difference.
scan_cost.per_kb_ratio_note: COST PER KILOBYTE, which removes the size confound entirely. This is the figure that describes the regime boundary; the raw ratio above is kept for completeness and is the more conservative one.

post_roundtrip.route_why: The route the user approved for EM-9/EM-10. PostBase.text caps at 63,206 chars so both the 60 KB and the 40 KB body fit. _require_post_owner (posts/router.py:30-33) means each account POSTs to its OWN username - no account can be used to write as another, which is also why the request set is spread rather than concentrated.

wire_sizes.note: The JSON envelope adds 41 bytes over the filler. The middleware scans the REQUEST BYTES, so every prefilter property and every per-KB figure below is against the WIRE size, not the text size.

post_roundtrip.tier_note: A DECLARED CONFIGURATION, exactly like the RBAC role. The tier decides which TIER_RATE_LIMITS entry applies to these accounts: pro is (1000, 3600) per user per path, which is why 1000 requests per arm can be driven at all - the free tier's (10, 3600) would 429 the tail. The row is created if absent because step4_campaign.seed_accounts seeds the ROLE but requires the TIER to pre-exist.

ceiling_derivation.note: Declared before any POST was issued. The scan half is the existing absolute ceiling; the allowance is anchored on EM-1's 2.80 ms serial figure for the cheapest authenticated DB round-trip in the programme's record, so it is not fitted to this run. It is a coarse guard on 'did the non-scan part explode', not the finding. Measured, it did: both arms breached it, because the non-scan work at concurrency 8 is roughly two orders of magnitude above the 2.80 ms serial figure this allowance was anchored on. That breach is a correct report of the endpoint, not a bad ceiling - and it is why the ceiling cannot stand in for the scan measurement.

seed_info.note: A DECLARED CONFIGURATION, like the tier. Full access was chosen because it is the grant a customer admin role would carry; a read-only role would measure the same endpoints under a different permission cache shape.

em9_miss_60kb.p99_note: ADR-0022 Rule 2. p99 requires pooled n >= 10000; this run reaches 1000, so the p99 figure is published as null rather than computed from a sample too small to carry it. Rule 3 still applies: the endpoint IS measured and it DOES gate - this is a reporting rule, not an exemption. The boundary between the two regimes is read from the RATIO, which neither an unresolvable tail nor a sample size can move.

em10_hit_40kb.p99_note: ADR-0022 Rule 2. p99 requires pooled n >= 10000; this run reaches 1000, so the p99 figure is published as null rather than computed from a sample too small to carry it. Rule 3 still applies: the endpoint IS measured and it DOES gate - this is a reporting rule, not an exemption. The boundary between the two regimes is read from the RATIO, which neither an unresolvable tail nor a sample size can move.

cleanup.note: The bodies are ~77 MB of rows at the default sizes. They are harness output, not application data, so they are removed at teardown and the count is recorded.

ratios.note: HIT over MISS on the each arm's own best_us. An additive constant leaves a DIFFERENCE invariant but not a RATIO, so the round-trip ratio is the scan ratio diluted by the non-scan work. The scan ratio is the one measuring the prefilter difference; the round-trip ratio is quoted so the dilution is a number here rather than a surprise for a reader who sees one arm and not the other.
ratios.dilution_note: roundtrip_ratio / scan_ratio, below 1 because the round-trip denominator carries the non-scan floor.
